text: Almost every smartphone on Earth runs on a design from one British company... that has never made a single chip!
Then how does it make money?
Arm, from Cambridge, sells blueprints. Apple, Samsung and Qualcomm pay a fee on every chip built from them.
Because whoever owns Arm holds the keys to over ninety-nine percent of smartphones.
Over three hundred billion Arm-based chips have shipped so far.
In twenty sixteen, Japan's SoftBank bought it for twenty-four billion pounds.
In twenty twenty, Nvidia offered forty billion dollars. Regulators in America, Britain and Europe pushed back.
They feared one chip giant would control the blueprints its rivals need. The deal died in twenty twenty-two.

Not bad, for a company that has never made a single chip.
